research_question: What is the effect of continuous intravenous infusion of loop diuretics compared with intravenous bolus injection on net weight loss in adults hospitalised with acute decompensated heart failure?
outcome_description: Net weight loss in kilograms from baseline to assessment timepoint (e.g., 24 to 72 hours or hospital discharge).
positive_direction: Greater net weight loss in the continuous infusion group compared to the intermittent bolus group.
search_queries: continuous infusion bolus furosemide acute decompensated heart failure weight loss trial
continuous versus bolus intravenous loop diuretics acute heart failure randomized trial
furosemide continuous infusion intermittent bolus clinical trial weight loss kg
inclusion_criteria: Adults hospitalized with acute decompensated heart failure receiving intravenous loop diuretics.
Randomized or controlled clinical trials comparing continuous intravenous infusion with intermittent intravenous bolus injection of loop diuretics.
Reporting quantitative data on net weight loss (in kg) or baseline and post-treatment weight.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, and theoretical papers are excluded).
No comparison between continuous intravenous infusion and intermittent bolus administration of loop diuretics.
No quantitative outcome data on net weight loss or body weight change from which an effect size can be calculated.
Completely unrelated to loop diuretic administration in hospitalized acute decompensated heart failure patients.
moderators_to_extract: Loop diuretic agent (e.g., furosemide, torsemide, bumetanide)
Assessment timepoint for weight loss (e.g., 24h, 48h, 72h, or discharge)
Dosing strategy (equimolar/isodose comparison vs. flexible/titrated dosing)
Mean baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (HFrEF vs. HFpEF/mixed)
Mean daily diuretic dose (furosemide equivalents in mg)
effect_size_note: Mean difference (MD) in kilograms of net weight loss (continuous minus bolus). Multi-arm trials with multiple continuous or bolus arms (e.g., high vs. low dose) should have arms of the same administration mode combined according to Cochrane guidelines.
